rationale:
Split into 12 children: six new lemmas (prefix dtc_bc_lc_fd_) and six comparator-accepted declarations reused with their identical frozen types.

Why split. The supplied proof rests on four large results of Simon Ch. 6. None of them is in the pinned SimonGMT library or exists as an accepted DAG declaration:
- the deformation theorem 5.1–5.4 (D);
- boundary rectifiability 6.3, with 3.14 in codimension 0 (BR);
- completeness of integer multiplicity (IM) currents 3.13 (CO);
- the slicing estimate 4.9–4.10 (SL).
Around them the proof has three self-contained arguments: the localisation at a good radius (step 3), the pigeonhole/diagonal extraction (step 5) and the series/globalisation step (steps 6–7). Each is a reusable statement with its own proof. One node cannot formalise all of this. The node is at depth 4 of 6, so the large results must become children now to keep one more split level.

Children (parent step → child):
1. localize — step 3 with (SL). Truncations T'_j = T_{φ(j)}⌞B_{t₀}: IM, spt ⊆ compact K, M(T'_j), M(∂T'_j) ≤ Λ, and T'_j = T_{φ(j)} on forms supported in W.
2. deformation — step 4 with (D). For compact K, Λ and ε > 0, a finite 𝒬 such that every IM A with spt A ⊆ K and M(A), M(∂A) ≤ Λ has A − Q − S = ∂R with Q ∈ 𝒬, R IM, M(R) + M(S) ≤ ε and spt R ⊆ cthickening(1, K); also ∂Q is IM with M(∂Q) ≤ cM(∂A).
3. cauchy_subseq — step 5. X_{φ(r+1)} − X_{φ(r)} − S_r = ∂R_r with M(R_r) + M(S_r) ≤ 2^{−r} and spt R_r ⊆ L.
4. series — steps 6(a)–(b), (CO) = Simon 3.13. A mass-summable series is a current, with mass and support bounds, and is IM if its terms are.
5. boundary_im — step 7(a), (BR). ∂R is IM for an IM (m+2)-current R in ℝ^P with compact support and finite masses: Simon 6.3 via 6.2 and 8.2, and Simon 3.14 when P = m + 2.
6. series_limit — steps 6–7. For every q, an IM decomposition Y − Z_q − S' = ∂R' with M_V(R') + M_V(S') ≤ 2·2^{−q}.
7.–12. Reused accepted declarations: cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub and dtc_mass_eq_measure (this node's inherited dependencies), cmc_fc_cs_diagonal_subseq, dtc_vanish_off_support, rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish, cmcs_slice_mass_integral.
The node keeps steps 1–2 and 8. Put a_j := inf of M_W(R) + M_W(S) over IM decompositions T − T_j − S = ∂R. Then a_j → 0 by the subsequence principle (Filter.tendsto_of_subseq_tendsto): apply localize, deformation, cauchy_subseq and series_limit to an arbitrary re-indexing ns → ∞. Finally choose near-optimal decompositions, using the default (0, T − T_j) when a_j = ∞.

subproblems.title: Localisation at a good radius: integer multiplicity truncations with uniformly bounded mass and boundary mass (Simon 7.2 proof; computation 4.9–4.11)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. Let T_j ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (j ∈ ℕ; GeometricCurrentOn univ n) be integer multiplicity currents (IsIntegerMultiplicity) such that sup_j (M_V(T_j) + M_V(∂T_j)) < ∞ for every bounded open V ⊆ ℝ^P, and let W ⊆ ℝ^P be bounded. Then there are a compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ, Λ ∈ [0, ∞) (NNReal) and integer multiplicity currents T'_j ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (j ∈ ℕ) such that for every j: spt T'_j ⊆ K, M(T'_j) ≤ Λ, M(∂T'_j) ≤ Λ, and T'_j(ω) = T_{φ(j)}(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Here M_V = massOn V (SimonGMT mass with the Euclidean coefficient norm), M = mass = M_{ℝ^P} and spt = GeometricCurrentOn.support.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (Ts : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)) (W : Set (Euclid P)), Bornology.IsBounded W → (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ts j)) → (∀ V : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen V → Bornology.IsBounded V → ⨆ j, ((Ts j).massOn V + (Ts j).boundary.massOn V) < ∞) → ∃ (K : Set (Euclid P)) (φ : ℕ → ℕ) (Λ : NNReal) (Ts' : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), IsCompact K ∧ StrictMono φ ∧ (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ts' j)) ∧ (∀ j, (Ts' j).support ⊆ K) ∧ (∀ j, (Ts' j).mass ≤ Λ ∧ (Ts' j).boundary.mass ≤ Λ) ∧ ∀ (j : ℕ) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) ⊆ W → Ts' j ω = Ts (φ j) ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2 (chapter-06.txt lines 2092–2100: "by 4.5(1),(2) and an argument as in 6.7(2) of Ch. 2 we can find a subsequence {T_j'} … with sup_j' M(∂(T_j'⌞W_i)) < ∞ … thus we can assume … spt T_j ⊆ W̄"), with the slice estimate 4.9 obtained as in Simon's proof of 4.9 through the identity 4.11 (lines 1355–1400). The parent writes ∂(T_j⌞B_t) = (∂T_j)⌞B_t + ⟨T_j, f, t−⟩ and bounds the two terms separately; the first term needs the Radon measure representation 2.7 of ∂T_j. Here the computation 4.11 is applied directly to ∂(T_j⌞B_t). It gives the same kind of bound, M(∂(T_j⌞B_t)) ≤ M_V(∂T_j) + c·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ_{T_j}({t − h < |x| < t}), without restricting ∂T_j. This is the only difference from the parent's step 3.

Notation. B_r := ball(0, r); |x| is the Euclidean norm; Hⁿ := μHE[n]. For a covector α, |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm). For a current X and a set G, M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum of ofReal X(ω) over test forms ω with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x ("admissible" forms), and M := M_{ℝ^P}. Applying the definition to ω and −ω (|−α| = |α|) gives |X(ω)| ≤ M_G(X) for admissible ω.
Siblings used: (IC) cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, parts (b) (the restriction of an IMRep to a Borel set represents an integer multiplicity current) and (d) (|⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for Hⁿ-a.e. x of the carrier); (MM) dtc_mass_eq_measure (M_G(T) = μ_R(G) for open G, R an IMRep of T, here U = ℝ^P); (SI) cmcs_slice_mass_integral (Simon 4.10); (SV) rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish.

1. (Setup.) W is bounded, so W ⊆ B_{r₀} for some r₀ > 0. Put V := B_{r₀+2}, which is open and bounded, and Λ₀ := sup_j (M_V(T_j) + M_V(∂T_j)) < ∞. In particular M_V(T_j) ≤ Λ₀ and M_V(∂T_j) ≤ Λ₀ for every j.
2. (Weights.) For each j fix an IMRep ℛ_j = (M_j, θ_j, ξ_j) representing T_j and put μ_j := ℛ_j.measure = θ_jHⁿ⌞M_j. By (MM), μ_j(G) = M_G(T_j) for every open G; so μ_j(V) ≤ Λ₀ and μ_j is finite on compact sets. By (IC)(d), |⟨α, ξ_j(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for μ_j-a.e. x and every n-covector α.
3. (Dini derivatives.) For t ∈ ℝ and h > 0 put A_j(t, h) := μ_j({x : t − h < |x| < t}) and D_j(t) := liminf_{h↓0} ofReal(h⁻¹)·A_j(t, h) ∈ [0, ∞] (liminf along 𝓝[>]0).
 (a) For t ∈ (r₀, r₀ + 1) and 0 < h < 1 the set {t − h < |x| < t} lies in V, so A_j(t, h) ≤ Λ₀ < ∞, and A_j(t, h) = F_j(t) − G_j(t − h) with F_j(s) := μ_j(B_s ∩ V) and G_j(s) := μ_j(closedBall(0, s) ∩ V), both finite and nondecreasing in s. Monotone functions are Borel, so t ↦ A_j(t, h) is Borel on (r₀, r₀ + 1) for each fixed h.
 (b) For fixed t, h ↦ A_j(t, h) is nondecreasing. Hence, for δ > 0 and every real h ∈ (0, ε), a rational h' ∈ [h/(1 + δ), h] satisfies h'⁻¹A_j(t, h') ≤ (1 + δ)h⁻¹A_j(t, h). So the liminf over rational h ↓ 0 is at most (1 + δ)D_j(t) for every δ > 0, and it is at least D_j(t) trivially. Thus D_j(t) = sup_k inf{h⁻¹A_j(t, h) : h ∈ ℚ ∩ (0, 1/k)} is Borel on (r₀, r₀ + 1).
 (c) By (SI) with μ := μ_j, f := |·| (continuous, hence measurable), W := ℝ^P, L := 1, m := D_j and (a, b) := (r₀, r₀ + 1) (the pointwise hypothesis holds with equality): ∫⁻_{(r₀, r₀+1)} D_j dt ≤ μ_j({r₀ < |x| < r₀ + 1}) ≤ μ_j(V) ≤ Λ₀.
4. (Good radius.) By (b) and Fatou's lemma, ∫⁻_{(r₀, r₀+1)} liminf_j D_j dt ≤ liminf_j ∫⁻_{(r₀, r₀+1)} D_j dt ≤ Λ₀ < ∞. Hence liminf_j D_j(t) < ∞ for a.e. t ∈ (r₀, r₀ + 1). This interval has positive measure, so we may fix such a t₀ ∈ (r₀, r₀ + 1); put C := liminf_j D_j(t₀) + 1 < ∞. Since D_j(t₀) < C for infinitely many j, there is a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ with D_{φ(j)}(t₀) ≤ C for every j.
5. (Restriction.) Put B := B_{t₀}, a Borel set. For each j apply (IC)(b) to ℛ_{φ(j)} and E := B. This gives an integer multiplicity current T'_j ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) represented by ℛ'_j := (M_{φ(j)} ∩ B, θ_{φ(j)}, ξ_{φ(j)}), i.e. T'_j(ω) = ∫_{M_{φ(j)} ∩ B} θ_{φ(j)}⟨ω, ξ_{φ(j)}⟩ dHⁿ. Its weight is ℛ'_j.measure = μ_{φ(j)}⌞B (restriction commutes with withDensity).
6. (Agreement on W.) If tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ B_{r₀} ⊆ B, then ω = 0 on M_{φ(j)} ∖ B, so T'_j(ω) = ∫_{M_{φ(j)}} θ_{φ(j)}⟨ω, ξ_{φ(j)}⟩ dHⁿ = T_{φ(j)}(ω).
7. (Support.) K := closedBall(0, r₀ + 1) is compact (ℝ^P is proper) and contains B. If tsupport ω is disjoint from K, then ω = 0 on B, so T'_j(ω) = 0. By (SV) (U = ℝ^P open, K compact), spt T'_j ⊆ K.
8. (Mass.) By (MM) applied to T'_j and ℛ'_j with G := ℝ^P: M(T'_j) = μ_{φ(j)}(B) ≤ μ_{φ(j)}(V) ≤ Λ₀.
9. (Boundary mass: computation 4.11.) Fix j and write T := T_{φ(j)}, μ := μ_{φ(j)}, ξ := ξ_{φ(j)}. Let η ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with |η(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. We bound ∂T'_j(η) = T'_j(dη).
 (a) Fix a C^∞ nondecreasing ψ : ℝ → [0, 1] with ψ = 0 on (−∞, 0] and ψ = 1 on [1, ∞) (e.g. Mathlib's Real.smoothTransition), and put c₁ := sup|ψ'| < ∞. For 0 < h < min(1, t₀/2) let γ_h(s) := 1 − ψ((s − t₀ + h)/h) and g_h(x) := γ_h(|x|). Then γ_h = 1 on (−∞, t₀ − h], γ_h = 0 on [t₀, ∞) and |γ_h'| ≤ c₁/h. Since γ_h is constant near 0 (t₀ − h > 0) and |·| is C^∞ on ℝ^P ∖ {0}, g_h is C^∞ on ℝ^P. Also 0 ≤ g_h ≤ 1, g_h = 1 on closedBall(0, t₀ − h), g_h = 0 off B, and Dg_h(x) = γ_h'(|x|)·x/|x| vanishes unless t₀ − h < |x| < t₀, with |Dg_h| ≤ c₁/h.
 (b) g_hη and g_h dη are test forms. The Leibniz rule for the exterior derivative of a function times a form gives d(g_hη) = dg_h ∧ η + g_h dη, where (dg ∧ η)(v₀, …, v_m) := Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i Dg(v_i)·η(v₀, …, v̂_i, …, v_m). Hence T(g_h dη) = T(d(g_hη)) − T(dg_h ∧ η) = ∂T(g_hη) − T(dg_h ∧ η). This is Simon's identity 4.11.
 (c) g_hη is admissible for M_V: tsupport(g_hη) ⊆ closedBall(0, t₀) ⊆ V and |g_hη| ≤ |η| ≤ 1. So |∂T(g_hη)| ≤ M_V(∂T) ≤ Λ₀.
 (d) For increasing I = (i₀ < ⋯ < i_m), (dg ∧ η)(e_I) = Σ_k (−1)^k ∂_{i_k}g·η(e_{I∖i_k}). By Cauchy–Schwarz, |(dg ∧ η)(e_I)|² ≤ (m + 1)Σ_k (∂_{i_k}g)²η(e_{I∖i_k})². Summing over I (each pair (i, J) with i ∉ J occurs at most once) gives |dg ∧ η| ≤ √(m+1)·|Dg|·|η| pointwise. With step 2: |T(dg_h ∧ η)| = |∫⟨dg_h ∧ η, ξ⟩ dμ| ≤ ∫|dg_h ∧ η| dμ ≤ √(m+1)·(c₁/h)·A_{φ(j)}(t₀, h).
 (e) T'_j(dη) = ∫_B ⟨dη, ξ⟩ dμ (step 5 and the weight formula), and T(g_h dη) = ∫ g_h⟨dη, ξ⟩ dμ. As h ↓ 0, g_h → 1_B pointwise: for |x| < t₀, g_h(x) = 1 once h ≤ t₀ − |x|; for |x| ≥ t₀, g_h(x) = 0. Also |g_h⟨dη, ξ⟩| ≤ |dη| μ-a.e., which is μ-integrable (bounded with compact support; μ is finite on compact sets). By dominated convergence (𝓝[>]0 is countably generated), T(g_h dη) → T'_j(dη).
 (f) By (b)–(d), |T(g_h dη)| ≤ Λ₀ + c₁√(m+1)·h⁻¹A_{φ(j)}(t₀, h) for all small h > 0. Take the liminf as h ↓ 0 and use (e): |∂T'_j(η)| ≤ Λ₀ + c₁√(m+1)·D_{φ(j)}(t₀) ≤ Λ₀ + c₁√(m+1)·C. Hence M(∂T'_j) ≤ Λ₁ := Λ₀ + c₁√(m+1)·C.
10. (Conclusion.) Put Λ := max(Λ₀, Λ₁) ∈ [0, ∞). Then K, φ, Λ and T'_j satisfy everything: T'_j is integer multiplicity (step 5), spt T'_j ⊆ K (step 7), M(T'_j) ≤ Λ (step 8), M(∂T'_j) ≤ Λ (step 9), and T'_j = T_{φ(j)} on forms supported in W (step 6). ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose r₀ with W ⊆ B_{r₀}, put V := B_{r₀+2} and Λ₀ := sup_j (M_V(T_j) + M_V(∂T_j)); the weights μ_j of integer multiplicity representations satisfy μ_j(V) ≤ Λ₀ (mass = weight).
D_j(t) := liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ_j({t−h<|x|<t}) is Borel on (r₀, r₀+1) and ∫_{r₀}^{r₀+1} D_j ≤ Λ₀ (Simon 4.10, cmcs_slice_mass_integral).
Fatou gives t₀ ∈ (r₀, r₀+1) with liminf_j D_j(t₀) < ∞, and a subsequence φ with D_{φ(j)}(t₀) ≤ C.
T'_j := T_{φ(j)}⌞B_{t₀}, by restricting the representation: integer multiplicity, equal to T_{φ(j)} on forms supported in W, spt ⊆ closedBall(0, r₀+1), M(T'_j) ≤ Λ₀.
Computation 4.11 with a radial cut-off g_h gives |T'_j(dη)| ≤ Λ₀ + c₁√(m+1)·D_{φ(j)}(t₀) for |η| ≤ 1, a uniform bound on M(∂T'_j).

subproblems.title: Finite nets from the scaled deformation theorem (Simon 5.1–5.4 and the proof of 7.2, (1)–(3))
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ with n := m + 1 < P. Then there is c ∈ [0, ∞) (NNReal) with the following property. For every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, every Λ ∈ [0, ∞) and every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is a finite set 𝒬 ⊆ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) such that every integer multiplicity A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with spt A ⊆ K, M(A) ≤ Λ and M(∂A) ≤ Λ admits Q ∈ 𝒬, R ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) and S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with: R and ∂Q are integer multiplicity; A − Q − S = ∂R (Simon: A − Q = ∂R + S); M(R) + M(S) ≤ ε; M(∂Q) ≤ c·M(∂A); and spt R ⊆ cthickening(1, K) = {x : dist(x, K) ≤ 1}. Masses are in [0, ∞], M = mass = M_{ℝ^P} with the Euclidean coefficient norm, and spt = GeometricCurrentOn.support.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ), m + 1 < P → ∃ c : NNReal, ∀ (K : Set (Euclid P)) (Λ : NNReal) (ε : ℝ≥0∞), IsCompact K → 0 < ε → ∃ 𝒬 : Set (GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), 𝒬.Finite ∧ ∀ A : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity A → A.support ⊆ K → A.mass ≤ Λ → A.boundary.mass ≤ Λ → ∃ Q ∈ 𝒬, ∃ (R : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 2)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), IsIntegerMultiplicity R ∧ IsIntegerMultiplicity Q.boundary ∧ A - Q - S = R.boundary ∧ R.mass + S.mass ≤ ε ∧ Q.boundary.mass ≤ c * A.boundary.mass ∧ R.support ⊆ cthickening 1 K
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2, (1)–(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 2047–2091). It rests on the scaled Deformation Theorem 5.3 (lines 1461–1480, proved by Lemma 5.4 and lines 1651–1935). Two conclusions are added to the parent's step 4. First, ∂Q is integer multiplicity with M(∂Q) ≤ cM(∂A); this comes from the bound M(∂P) ≤ CM(∂T) of 5.1/5.3, is what Simon's proof of 6.2 uses, and is needed by the sibling boundary_im. Second, spt R stays in the fixed compact set cthickening(1, K). Two parts of the parent's step 4 are dropped because nothing downstream uses them: the support of S, and integer multiplicity of the net elements (Q cancels in step 5 of the parent). As in the parent, S is just a current.

Cited result (D): Simon 5.1/5.3, used for n = m + 1 ≥ 1 and ℓ := P − n ≥ 1, the range n, ℓ ∈ {1, 2, …} of Simon §5. There is C = C(n, ℓ) ≥ 1 such that for every T ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with M(T) + M(∂T) < ∞ and every σ > 0 we have T − P_σ = ∂R + S, where:
 • P_σ = Σ_{F ∈ 𝓛_n(σ)} β_F[[F]];
 • M(P_σ) ≤ CM(T), M(∂P_σ) ≤ CM(∂T), M(R) ≤ CσM(T) and M(S) ≤ CσM(∂T);
 • spt P_σ ∪ spt R ⊆ {x : dist(x, spt T) < 2√P σ} and spt ∂P_σ ∪ spt S ⊆ {x : dist(x, spt ∂T) < 2√P σ};
 • if T is integer multiplicity, P_σ and R can be chosen integer multiplicity, with all β_F ∈ ℤ.
Here 𝓛_n(σ) is the set of closed n-faces of the cubical decomposition ⋃_{z∈ℤ^P} σ(z + [0,1]^P). [[F]] ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) is integration over F with the coordinate orientation e_F of F (Simon 2.2), [[F]](ω) = ∫_F ⟨ω, e_F⟩ dHⁿ, and Hⁿ(F) = σⁿ.
Siblings used: (IC) cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub (c): differences, hence finite integer combinations, of integer multiplicity currents are integer multiplicity. (MM) dtc_mass_eq_measure.

1. (Constant.) Let c := C, the constant of (D) for n and ℓ = P − n ≥ 1. Fix K compact, Λ ≥ 0 and ε ∈ (0, ∞].
2. (Scale.) Choose σ > 0 with 2√P σ ≤ 1 and 2CσΛ ≤ ε. If ε = ∞, only the first condition is needed.
3. (Candidate set.) K₁ := cthickening(1, K) is compact. Let ℱ := {F ∈ 𝓛_n(σ) : F ⊆ K₁}. ℱ is finite, because K₁ is bounded and only finitely many cubes σ(z + [0,1]^P) meet a bounded set. Let N := ⌊CΛσ^{−n}⌋ and 𝒬 := {Σ_{F∈ℱ} b_F[[F]] : b ∈ ℤ^ℱ, |b_F| ≤ N for every F}. This is a finite set with at most (2N + 1)^{#ℱ} elements, and it depends only on K, Λ, ε, n and P.
4. (Deformation.) Let A be integer multiplicity with spt A ⊆ K, M(A) ≤ Λ and M(∂A) ≤ Λ. Then M(A) + M(∂A) < ∞. So (D), with T := A and the σ of step 2, gives an integer multiplicity P := P_σ = Σ β_F[[F]] (β_F ∈ ℤ), an integer multiplicity R and a current S with A − P = ∂R + S, i.e. A − P − S = ∂R.
5. (Small error.) M(R) + M(S) ≤ CσM(A) + CσM(∂A) ≤ 2CσΛ ≤ ε.
6. (Support of R.) spt R ⊆ {x : dist(x, spt A) < 2√Pσ} ⊆ {x : dist(x, K) < 1} ⊆ K₁, because spt A ⊆ K and 2√Pσ ≤ 1. If spt A = ∅, the middle set is empty.
7. (P ∈ 𝒬.)
 (a) Two distinct faces of 𝓛_n(σ) meet in a set of dimension < n, hence of Hⁿ-measure 0, and the relative interior of a face meets no other n-face. So P = τ(⋃_{β_F≠0} relint F, |β_F|, sign(β_F)e_F). By (MM), M(P) = Σ_F |β_F|Hⁿ(F) = Σ_F |β_F|σⁿ; this is the identity M(P) = Σ|β_F|ρⁿ of Simon's (3). As M(P) ≤ CM(A) ≤ CΛ < ∞, only finitely many β_F are nonzero, and each satisfies |β_F| ≤ CΛσ^{−n}, i.e. |β_F| ≤ N.
 (b) Let β_F ≠ 0 and x ∈ relint F. Take ω := φ·e^F, where φ ≥ 0 is a bump function at x supported away from the other faces with nonzero coefficient and e^F is the coordinate covector dual to e_F. Then P(ω) = β_F∫_F φ dHⁿ ≠ 0, so x ∈ spt P. Hence relint F ⊆ spt P, and F ⊆ spt P because spt P is closed. By (D), spt P ⊆ {dist(·, spt A) < 2√Pσ} ⊆ K₁, so F ∈ ℱ.
 Thus Q := P = Σ_{F∈ℱ} β_F[[F]] ∈ 𝒬.
8. (∂Q.) By Stokes' theorem on the cube F, ∂[[F]] = Σ_G ±[[G]] over the (n − 1)-faces G of F; for n = 1, ∂[[F]] = δ_b − δ_a when F is the segment from a to b. So ∂Q = Σ_{G∈𝓛_{n−1}(σ)} γ_G[[G]] with γ_G ∈ ℤ and only finitely many γ_G ≠ 0. Each [[G]] is integer multiplicity: it is τ(G, 1, e_G), where G lies in an (n − 1)-plane, so G is countably (n − 1)-rectifiable with that plane as approximate tangent space at every relative interior point, and e_G is a unit orientation of the plane. For n − 1 = 0, G is a point, H⁰ is counting measure and e_G = 1. By (IC)(c), with −B = (B − B) − B and A + B = A − (−B), every finite integer combination of integer multiplicity currents is integer multiplicity. Hence ∂Q is integer multiplicity. By (D), M(∂Q) = M(∂P_σ) ≤ CM(∂A) = c·M(∂A).
9. (Conclusion.) We have Q ∈ 𝒬, R and ∂Q integer multiplicity, A − Q − S = ∂R, M(R) + M(S) ≤ ε, M(∂Q) ≤ c·M(∂A) and spt R ⊆ cthickening(1, K). ∎
proof_key_steps: c := C(n, ℓ) from the deformation theorem 5.3 (n = m + 1 ≥ 1, ℓ = P − n ≥ 1); choose σ with 2√Pσ ≤ 1 and 2CσΛ ≤ ε.
𝒬 := integer combinations Σ_{F∈ℱ} b_F[[F]] with |b_F| ≤ CΛσ^{−n}, over the finitely many σ-grid n-faces F ⊆ cthickening(1, K).
For A, 5.3 gives A − P − S = ∂R with P and R integer multiplicity, M(R) + M(S) ≤ 2CσΛ ≤ ε and spt R ⊆ cthickening(1, K).
M(P) = Σ|β_F|σⁿ ≤ CΛ, and every face with β_F ≠ 0 lies in spt P ⊆ cthickening(1, K); so P ∈ 𝒬.
∂P is an integer combination of (n − 1)-faces, hence integer multiplicity, and M(∂P) ≤ CM(∂A).

subproblems.title: A flat-Cauchy subsequence from finite nets, with real error currents and supports in a fixed compact set (Simon 7.2, (5))
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, let L ⊆ ℝ^P be compact and let X_j ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (j ∈ ℕ). Suppose the following holds for every ε ∈ (0, ∞]: there is a finite set 𝒬 ⊆ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) such that for every j there are Q ∈ 𝒬, an integer multiplicity R ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) with spt R ⊆ L, and a current S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), with X_j − Q − S = ∂R and M(R) + M(S) ≤ ε. Then there is a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ such that for every r ∈ ℕ there are an integer multiplicity R_r ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) with spt R_r ⊆ L and a current S_r ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with X_{φ(r+1)} − X_{φ(r)} − S_r = ∂R_r and M(R_r) + M(S_r) ≤ 2^{−r}, written (2⁻¹)^r in [0, ∞]. M = mass = M_{ℝ^P}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (L : Set (Euclid P)) (X : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), IsCompact L → (∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ 𝒬 : Set (GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), 𝒬.Finite ∧ ∀ j, ∃ Q ∈ 𝒬, ∃ (R : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 2)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), IsIntegerMultiplicity R ∧ R.support ⊆ L ∧ X j - Q - S = R.boundary ∧ R.mass + S.mass ≤ ε) → ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∀ r, ∃ (R : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 2)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), IsIntegerMultiplicity R ∧ R.support ⊆ L ∧ X (φ (r + 1)) - X (φ r) - S = R.boundary ∧ R.mass + S.mass ≤ (2⁻¹ : ℝ≥0∞) ^ r
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2 (chapter-06.txt lines 2102–2116: "apply (1) with ε = 1, 1/2, 1/4 etc. to extract a subsequence {T_{j_r}} … such that d_W̃(T_{j_{r+1}}, T_{j_r}) < 2^{−r} and hence (5) T_{j_{r+1}} − T_{j_r} = ∂R_r + S_r … M(R_r) + M(S_r) ≤ 1/2^r"). As in the parent, the error currents S need not be integer multiplicity. The condition spt R ⊆ L is carried along for the sibling series_limit.
Siblings used: (IC) cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub (c); (DG) cmc_fc_cs_diagonal_subseq; (VO) dtc_vanish_off_support; (SV) rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish.

1. (Nets.) For r ∈ ℕ put ε_r := 2^{−(r+1)} > 0. By hypothesis there is a finite 𝒬_r, and for every j a choice of Q_r(j) ∈ 𝒬_r, an integer multiplicity R_{r,j} with spt R_{r,j} ⊆ L and a current S_{r,j}, with X_j − Q_r(j) − S_{r,j} = ∂R_{r,j} and M(R_{r,j}) + M(S_{r,j}) ≤ 2^{−(r+1)}.
2. (Relation.) For r, j, l ∈ ℕ let C(r, j, l) be the statement: there are an integer multiplicity R with spt R ⊆ L and a current S with X_j − X_l − S = ∂R and M(R) + M(S) ≤ 2^{−r}.
3. (Pigeonhole.) Let r ∈ ℕ and let I ⊆ ℕ be infinite. Then I ⊆ ⋃_{Q∈𝒬_r} {j ∈ I : Q_r(j) = Q}, a finite union. So for some Q the set J := {j ∈ I : Q_r(j) = Q} ⊆ I is infinite.
4. (Pairs in J.) Let j, l ∈ J, so Q_r(j) = Q_r(l) = Q. Put R := R_{r,j} − R_{r,l} and S := S_{r,j} − S_{r,l}.
 (a) R is integer multiplicity by (IC)(c), since ℝ^P is open.
 (b) For every ω, evaluate the two decompositions of step 1 at ω and subtract: X_j(ω) − X_l(ω) − (S_{r,j}(ω) − S_{r,l}(ω)) = ∂R_{r,j}(ω) − ∂R_{r,l}(ω). The contract's subtraction acts pointwise, ∂ is linear, and currents are determined by their values, so X_j − X_l − S = ∂R.
 (c) If tsupport ω is disjoint from L, it is disjoint from spt R_{r,j} and from spt R_{r,l}. So R_{r,j}(ω) = R_{r,l}(ω) = 0 by (VO), and R(ω) = 0. By (SV), with L compact, spt R ⊆ L.
 (d) For any currents A, B and any set G, M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B). Indeed, for admissible ω, ofReal(A(ω) − B(ω)) ≤ ofReal A(ω) + ofReal B(−ω), and −ω is admissible (|−α| = |α|, tsupport(−ω) = tsupport ω). Hence M(R) + M(S) ≤ (M(R_{r,j}) + M(S_{r,j})) + (M(R_{r,l}) + M(S_{r,l})) ≤ 2·2^{−(r+1)} = 2^{−r}.
 So C(r, j, l) holds for all j, l ∈ J, including j = l.
5. (Diagonal.) By steps 3 and 4 the relation C satisfies the hypothesis of (DG). (DG) gives a strictly increasing φ with C(r, φ(r + 1), φ(r)) for every r, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: For each r, choose 2^{−(r+1)}-nets 𝒬_r and decompositions X_j − Q_r(j) − S_{r,j} = ∂R_{r,j}.
Pigeonhole: every infinite I ⊆ ℕ contains an infinite J on which j ↦ Q_r(j) is constant.
For j, l ∈ J, subtract: X_j − X_l − (S_{r,j} − S_{r,l}) = ∂(R_{r,j} − R_{r,l}), integer multiplicity, support in L, total mass ≤ 2^{−r}.
The diagonal lemma cmc_fc_cs_diagonal_subseq gives a strictly increasing φ whose consecutive terms are related.

subproblems.title: Mass-summable series of currents in ℝ^P: the sum is a current with mass and support bounds, and is integer multiplicity if the terms are (Simon 3.13)
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, d := k + 1, and let X_i ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) (i ∈ ℕ) with Σ_i M(X_i) < ∞ (sum in [0, ∞], M = mass = M_{ℝ^P}). Then there is Y ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with the following properties: for every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^P) the real series Σ_i X_i(ω) converges to Y(ω) (HasSum); M(Y) ≤ Σ_i M(X_i); spt Y ⊆ closure(⋃_i spt X_i); and if every X_i is integer multiplicity, then so is Y.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (X : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (k + 1)), ∑' i, (X i).mass < ∞ → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (k + 1), (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (k + 1), HasSum (fun i => X i ω) (Y ω)) ∧ Y.mass ≤ ∑' i, (X i).mass ∧ Y.support ⊆ closure (⋃ i, (X i).support) ∧ ((∀ i, IsIntegerMultiplicity (X i)) → IsIntegerMultiplicity Y)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 6(a)–(b) of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2, lines 2117–2124: "by 3.13 we can define integer multiplicity R^{(ℓ)}, S^{(ℓ)} by the M-absolutely convergent series"), and Simon's Lemma 3.13 with its printed proof (chapter-06.txt lines 897–937), here with U = ℝ^P and the global mass M = M_{ℝ^P}.
Notation. For ω ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^P), ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| < ∞, with |·| the Euclidean coefficient norm. Hᵈ := μHE[d]. Siblings used: (IC) cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub (a), (c); (MM) dtc_mass_eq_measure; (VO) dtc_vanish_off_support.

1. (Evaluation bound.) For a current X with M(X) < ∞ and any ω, |X(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖M(X). If ‖ω‖ = 0 then ω = 0, because |α| = 0 forces all coefficients α(e_I) (I increasing) to vanish and these determine α; then X(ω) = 0. Otherwise ±ω/‖ω‖ are admissible for M, so ±X(ω) ≤ ‖ω‖M(X).
2. (Pointwise sum.) Let s := Σ_i M(X_i) < ∞; then every M(X_i) < ∞. For each ω, Σ_i |X_i(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖s < ∞, so Σ_i X_i(ω) converges absolutely. Let Y(ω) be its sum; then HasSum (i ↦ X_i(ω)) (Y(ω)).
3. (Y is a current.) Y is linear, as a sum of linear functionals. Continuity in Simon's sequential sense (6.2.1): suppose ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^d(ℝ^P), i.e. the supports lie in a fixed compact set and all derivatives tend to 0 uniformly. Then sup_x ‖ω_j(x)‖_op → 0. Also |α| ≤ (number of increasing I)^{1/2}·‖α‖_op, since |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖_op. So ‖ω_j‖ → 0 and |Y(ω_j)| ≤ ‖ω_j‖s → 0.
4. (Mass.) For admissible ω, ofReal Y(ω) = ofReal(Σ_i X_i(ω)) ≤ Σ_i ofReal X_i(ω) ≤ Σ_i M(X_i), because ofReal is subadditive and continuous. Taking the supremum, M(Y) ≤ s. The same argument applied to a tail series gives M(Y − Σ_{i<N} X_i) ≤ Σ_{i≥N} M(X_i).
5. (Support.) Let F := closure(⋃_i spt X_i) and x ∉ F, and choose r > 0 with closedBall(x, 2r) ∩ F = ∅. If tsupport ω ⊆ B_r(x), then tsupport ω is disjoint from every spt X_i, so X_i(ω) = 0 by (VO) and Y(ω) = 0. B_r(x) is open with compact closure, so it is one of the sets whose union is the zero region of Y. Hence x ∉ spt Y, and spt Y ⊆ F.
6. (Integer multiplicity: Simon 3.13.) Assume every X_i is integer multiplicity.
 (a) The partial sums Z_N := X_0 + ⋯ + X_{N−1} are integer multiplicity. By (IC)(c), 0 = B − B, −B = 0 − B and A + B = A − (−B) are integer multiplicity whenever A and B are. By step 4, M(Y − Z_N) ≤ Σ_{i≥N} M(X_i) → 0. In particular (Z_N) is Cauchy for M.
 (b) Write Z_N = τ(M_N, θ_N, ξ_N), with θ_N := 0 and ξ_N := 0 off M_N. Let N ≤ N'. On M_N ∩ M_{N'} the approximate tangent spaces of M_N and M_{N'} agree Hᵈ-a.e. by (IC)(a), so ξ_{N'} = ±ξ_N there. Z_{N'} − Z_N is represented as in the construction of (IC)(c): multiplicity |θ_{N'} ∓ θ_N| on the overlap and θ_{N'}, resp. θ_N, off it. Its weight is |θ_{N'}ξ_{N'} − θ_Nξ_N|Hᵈ, where |aζ| = |a| for a unit simple d-vector ζ. So by (MM), M(Z_{N'} − Z_N) = ∫|θ_{N'}ξ_{N'} − θ_Nξ_N| dHᵈ =: ε(N, N'); this is Simon's (1). By (a), ε(N, N') → 0 as N → ∞, uniformly in N' ≥ N.
 (c) Since |ξ_N| = 1 on M_N and θ_N ≥ 0, ∫|θ_{N'} − θ_N| dHᵈ ≤ ε(N, N') (Simon's (2)). So θ_N → θ in L¹(Hᵈ) for some θ. A subsequence converges Hᵈ-a.e., so θ is integer valued with θ ≥ 0. Put M_+ := {θ > 0}. Since |θ_N − θ| ≥ 1 on (M_+ ∖ M_N) ∪ (M_N ∖ M_+), we get Hᵈ((M_+ ∖ M_N) ∪ (M_N ∖ M_+)) ≤ ∫|θ_N − θ| dHᵈ → 0 (Simon's (3)). In particular M_+ lies in ⋃_N M_N up to an Hᵈ-null set, so it is countably d-rectifiable, and ∫_{M_+} θ dHᵈ < ∞.
 (d) From (b) and (c), ∫θ_{N'}|ξ_{N'} − ξ_N| dHᵈ ≤ 2ε(N, N'). So ξ_N converges in L¹(Hᵈ⌞M_+) to a function ξ that is simple with |ξ| = 1 on M_+. By (c) and (IC)(a), T_xM_+ = T_xM_N for x ∈ M_+ outside a set whose measure tends to 0, and ξ_N(x) orients T_xM_N. Hence ξ(x) orients T_xM_+ for Hᵈ-a.e. x ∈ M_+, and Y' := τ(M_+, θ, ξ) is an integer multiplicity current.
 (e) M(Z_N − Y') ≤ ∫|θ_Nξ_N − θξ| dHᵈ → 0 (Simon: "M_W(T_P − T) → 0"). Both Y and Y' are limits of Z_N in mass, hence weakly, so Y = Y'. Thus Y is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: |X(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖M(X), so Σ X_i(ω) converges absolutely; Y(ω) := Σ X_i(ω) is linear and sequentially continuous, so it is a current.
M(Y) ≤ Σ M(X_i), and spt Y ⊆ closure(⋃ spt X_i) because each X_i vanishes on forms supported off its support.
If the X_i are integer multiplicity, the partial sums Z_N are integer multiplicity and M(Y − Z_N) → 0.
Simon 3.13: θ_Nξ_N is Cauchy in L¹(Hᵈ); θ_N → θ integer valued, the carriers converge, ξ_N → ξ orients T_xM_+; so Y = τ(M_+, θ, ξ).

subproblems.title: Boundary rectifiability for a compactly supported integer multiplicity (m+2)-current of finite mass in ℝ^P (Simon 6.3 via 6.2 and 8.2; Simon 3.14 in codimension zero)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ with m + 1 < P, and let R ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) be an integer multiplicity current with compact support, M(R) < ∞ and M(∂R) < ∞ (M = mass = M_{ℝ^P}). Then ∂R ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) is integer multiplicity.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (R : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 2)), m + 1 < P → IsIntegerMultiplicity R → IsCompact R.support → R.mass < ∞ → R.boundary.mass < ∞ → IsIntegerMultiplicity R.boundary
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Theorem 6.3, the Boundary Rectifiability Theorem (chapter-06.txt lines 1994–2001: "A direct consequence of 6.2 above and the Compactness 3.11"). By Remark 6.4 only the case ∂T_j = 0 of 3.11 is needed, which is Theorem 8.2 for cycles (lines 2303–2321). In codimension zero the source is Simon 3.14 (lines 939–1132), as Simon states in the introduction to §6 (lines 1931–1937: "Notice that in the case k = 0, this has already been established in 3.14").
This is the result (BR) cited in step 7(a) of the parent proof, applied there to the (n+1)-current R^{(q)}, n = m + 1. Correction to the parent's remark that every citation stays in codimension ≥ 1: the codimension of R is P − m − 2 ≥ 0, and it is 0 when P = m + 2. That case is Simon 3.14 (Case 2 below). The hypotheses "spt R compact" and "M(R) < ∞" hold in the parent's application. They put us in the first case of Simon's proof of 6.2 (U = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, M(T), M(∂T) < ∞).
Sibling used: (DF) dtc_bc_lc_fd_deformation. Cited results: Simon 8.2 (a weak limit of integer multiplicity currents with integer multiplicity boundaries and locally bounded masses is integer multiplicity; used for cycles); Simon 3.14, with Ch. 3, 4.1–4.3 (De Giorgi) and Ch. 6, 2.35 and 3.15.
Notation: d := m + 2. For a current X with M(X) < ∞ and a form ω, |X(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖M(X), where ‖ω‖ := sup_x|ω(x)|. To see this, apply the definition of M to ±ω/‖ω‖; if ‖ω‖ = 0 then ω = 0.

Case 1: P ≥ m + 3 (codimension P − d ≥ 1).
1. (DF) with m' := m + 1 (so m' + 1 = d < P) gives a constant c. Put K := spt R (compact) and Λ := max(M(R), M(∂R)) ∈ [0, ∞). For k ≥ 1, apply (DF) with K, Λ and ε := 1/k to A := R. This gives Q_k, an integer multiplicity R_k ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) and S_k ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with R − Q_k − S_k = ∂R_k, M(R_k) + M(S_k) ≤ 1/k, ∂Q_k integer multiplicity and M(∂Q_k) ≤ cM(∂R). This is the first case of Simon's proof of 6.2: T − P_k = ∂R_k + S_k with M(R_k) + M(S_k) → 0 and M(∂P_k) ≤ cM(∂T).
2. (Q_k ⇀ R.) For ω ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^P), R(ω) − Q_k(ω) = S_k(ω) + R_k(dω). So |R(ω) − Q_k(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖M(S_k) + ‖dω‖M(R_k) ≤ (‖ω‖ + ‖dω‖)/k → 0.
3. (∂Q_k ⇀ ∂R.) For η ∈ 𝒟^{d−1}(ℝ^P), ∂Q_k(η) = Q_k(dη) → R(dη) = ∂R(η).
4. (Compactness for cycles.) The currents ∂Q_k ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) are integer multiplicity, their boundaries ∂(∂Q_k) = 0 are integer multiplicity, and sup_k (M_W(∂Q_k) + M_W(∂∂Q_k)) ≤ cM(∂R) < ∞ for every W. Apply Simon's Theorem 8.2 in U = ℝ^P (trivial when the dimension is 0) to the sequence ∂Q_k, whose weak limit is ∂R by step 3. Hence ∂R is integer multiplicity.

Case 2: P = m + 2 (codimension 0). Put n := m + 1, so P = n + 1 and R ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^{n+1}) is integer multiplicity with M(∂R) < ∞. This is the situation of Simon 3.14 with U = ℝ^{n+1}, which says that T := ∂R is integer multiplicity. Its printed proof runs as follows.
5. R = τ(V, θ, ξ) with V Lebesgue measurable and ξ = ±e₁∧⋯∧e_{n+1}. Put θ̃ := θ where ξ = +e₁∧⋯∧e_{n+1}, θ̃ := −θ where ξ = −e₁∧⋯∧e_{n+1}, and θ̃ := 0 off V. Then R(a dx¹∧⋯∧dx^{n+1}) = ∫ aθ̃ dL^{n+1}, θ̃ is integer valued, M_W(R) = ∫_W|θ̃| and M_W(T) = ∫_W|Dθ̃|. So θ̃ ∈ BV_loc (Simon 2.35 and 3.15).
6. Let U_j := {θ̃ ≥ j} for j ∈ ℤ and V_j := ℝ^{n+1} ∖ U_j for j ≤ 0. Then θ̃ = Σ_{j≥1} χ_{U_j} − Σ_{j≤0} χ_{V_j}. So R = Σ_{j≥1}[[U_j]] − Σ_{j≤0}[[V_j]] and T = ∂R = Σ_{j∈ℤ} ∂[[U_j]] (Simon's (3) and (4)).
7. Take ψ_j ∈ C^∞(ℝ) with ψ_j = 0 on (−∞, j − 1 + ε], ψ_j = 1 on [j − ε, ∞) and 0 ≤ ψ_j' ≤ 1 + 3ε, so that χ_{U_j} = ψ_j ∘ θ̃. Mollifying θ̃ gives ∫ div g Σ_{j=M}^{N} χ_{U_j} ≤ (1 + 3ε)∫ a|Dθ̃| for |g| ≤ a (Simon's (5) and (6)). Hence each U_j has locally finite perimeter and M_W(∂[[U_j]]) ≤ M_W(T). Moreover, for R_N := Σ_{j=1}^{N}[[U_j]] − Σ_{j=−N}^{0}[[V_j]] and T_N := ∂R_N, ∫ a d‖T_N‖ ≤ ∫ a d‖T‖ (Simon's (7)).
8. By De Giorgi's theorem (Ch. 3, 4.1–4.3, chapter-03.txt lines 551–606), ∂[[U_j]] is integration over the reduced boundary ∂*U_j against the inward unit normal ν_j: ∂[[U_j]](⋆g) = −∫_{∂*U_j} ν_j·g dHⁿ. Here ∂*U_j is countably n-rectifiable, with approximate tangent space ν_j(x)^⊥ at Hⁿ-a.e. point. Since U_{j+1} ⊆ U_j, ν_j = ν_k on ∂*U_j ∩ ∂*U_k (Ch. 3, 4.3(∗)). So with ν := ν_j on ∂*U_j and h_N := Σ_{|j|≤N} χ_{∂*U_j}, T_N is represented by the integer multiplicity h_N on ⋃_j ∂*U_j with the orientation ⋆ν dual to ν, and ∫ a d‖T_N‖ = Σ_{|j|≤N} ∫_{∂*U_j} a dHⁿ (Simon's (8)).
9. Letting N → ∞ in (7)–(8) gives ‖T‖ ≥ Σ_j ‖∂[[U_j]]‖ = h·Hⁿ⌞⋃_j ∂*U_j, where h := Σ_j χ_{∂*U_j} is integer valued and locally Hⁿ-integrable (∫_W h dHⁿ ≤ M_W(T) < ∞). The reverse inequality follows from (4). Hence the series Σ_j ∂[[U_j]] converges in mass to T, and T = τ(⋃_j ∂*U_j, h, ⋆ν). So ∂R = T is integer multiplicity. ∎

Q_k ⇀ R, hence ∂Q_k ⇀ ∂R.
Simon 8.2 for the integer multiplicity cycles ∂Q_k (Remark 6.4: only the cycle case of 3.11 is needed) shows that ∂R is integer multiplicity.

Case P = m + 2 (codimension 0), Simon 3.14: R = [[θ̃]] with θ̃ ∈ BV integer valued, ∂R = Σ_j ∂[[{θ̃ ≥ j}]] with additive masses, and by De Giorgi each ∂[[U_j]] has multiplicity one on the reduced boundary; so ∂R is integer multiplicity.

subproblems.title: Summing a 2^{−r}-telescoping flat decomposition against the weak limit on V, with an integer multiplicity error current (Simon 7.2, series step; Simon 6.3)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ with n := m + 1 < P. Let V, L ⊆ ℝ^P with L compact, let Λ ∈ [0, ∞), and let X_r, Z_r, Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), R_r ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) and S_r ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (r ∈ ℕ). Assume: Y and every Z_r are integer multiplicity; M(X_r) ≤ Λ for every r; for every r, R_r is integer multiplicity, spt R_r ⊆ L, X_{r+1} − X_r − S_r = ∂R_r and M(R_r) + M(S_r) ≤ 2^{−r}; and for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ V, Z_r(ω) = X_r(ω) for all r and X_r(ω) → Y(ω) as r → ∞. Then for every q ∈ ℕ there are integer multiplicity R' ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) and S' ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with Y − Z_q − S' = ∂R' and M_V(R') + M_V(S') ≤ 2·2^{−q} (in [0, ∞]; M = mass = M_{ℝ^P}, M_V = massOn V).

Source: steps 6–7 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2 (chapter-06.txt lines 2117–2131: "by 3.13 we can define integer multiplicity R^{(ℓ)}, S^{(ℓ)} by the M-absolutely convergent series R^{(ℓ)} = Σ_{r≥ℓ} R_r, S^{(ℓ)} = Σ_{r≥ℓ} S_r; then M(R^{(ℓ)}) + M(S^{(ℓ)}) ≤ 2^{−ℓ+1} and (from (5)) T − T_{j_ℓ} = ∂R^{(ℓ)} + S^{(ℓ)}"). In the parent, X_r = T'_{j_r} (the localised currents), Z_r = T_{j_r}, Y = T and V is the region where they agree. As in the parent, the identity holds only on forms supported in V. A global integer multiplicity error current comes from boundary rectifiability (parent step 7). The bound M(∂R^{(q)}) < ∞ is obtained by evaluating the telescoping identity directly; this is the same estimate that the parent obtains from lower semicontinuity.
Siblings used: (SE) dtc_bc_lc_fd_series; (BR) dtc_bc_lc_fd_boundary_im; (IC) cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub (c). For a current X with M(X) < ∞ and ω with |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, |X(ω)| ≤ M(X): apply the definition of M to ω and to −ω.

Fix q.
1. (Masses.) M(R_r) ≤ 2^{−r} and M(S_r) ≤ 2^{−r}, and Σ_{i≥0} 2^{−(q+i)} = 2·2^{−q} < ∞.
2. (Series.) Apply (SE) in degree m + 2 = (m + 1) + 1 to (R_{q+i})_i. It gives R^{(q)} ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) with HasSum (i ↦ R_{q+i}(ω')) (R^{(q)}(ω')) for every ω' and M(R^{(q)}) ≤ Σ_i M(R_{q+i}). Also spt R^{(q)} ⊆ closure(⋃_i spt R_{q+i}) ⊆ L, since L is compact, hence closed. R^{(q)} is integer multiplicity because every R_r is. Apply (SE) in degree m + 1 to (S_{q+i})_i. It gives S^{(q)} ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with HasSum (i ↦ S_{q+i}(ω)) (S^{(q)}(ω)) and M(S^{(q)}) ≤ Σ_i M(S_{q+i}) < ∞.
3. (Telescoping.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). For every r, evaluating X_{r+1} − X_r − S_r = ∂R_r at ω gives R_r(dω) = X_{r+1}(ω) − X_r(ω) − S_r(ω). Summing over r = q, …, q + N − 1 gives X_{q+N}(ω) = X_q(ω) + Σ_{i<N} R_{q+i}(dω) + Σ_{i<N} S_{q+i}(ω). By step 2 and ∂R^{(q)}(ω) = R^{(q)}(dω):
 (#) X_{q+N}(ω) → X_q(ω) + ∂R^{(q)}(ω) + S^{(q)}(ω) as N → ∞, for every ω.
4. (Finite boundary mass.) Let ω be admissible for M, i.e. |ω(x)| ≤ 1. Then |X_r(ω)| ≤ M(X_r) ≤ Λ and −S^{(q)}(ω) ≤ M(S^{(q)}). By (#), X_q(ω) + ∂R^{(q)}(ω) + S^{(q)}(ω) = lim_N X_{q+N}(ω) ≤ Λ, so ∂R^{(q)}(ω) ≤ 2Λ + M(S^{(q)}). Hence M(∂R^{(q)}) ≤ 2Λ + M(S^{(q)}) < ∞.
5. (Boundary rectifiability.) spt R^{(q)} is closed, being the complement of the open zero region, and it lies in the compact set L, so it is compact. Also M(R^{(q)}) < ∞ (step 2), M(∂R^{(q)}) < ∞ (step 4) and m + 1 < P. By (BR), ∂R^{(q)} is integer multiplicity.
6. (Identity on V.) Let tsupport ω ⊆ V. Then X_r(ω) → Y(ω), so by (#) and uniqueness of limits, Y(ω) = X_q(ω) + ∂R^{(q)}(ω) + S^{(q)}(ω) = Z_q(ω) + ∂R^{(q)}(ω) + S^{(q)}(ω), using Z_q(ω) = X_q(ω). (★)
7. (The decomposition.) Put R' := R^{(q)} and S' := Y − Z_q − ∂R^{(q)}. R' is integer multiplicity (step 2). S' is integer multiplicity by (IC)(c) applied twice, since Y, Z_q and ∂R^{(q)} are integer multiplicity. For every ω, (Y − Z_q − S')(ω) = Y(ω) − Z_q(ω) − (Y(ω) − Z_q(ω) − ∂R^{(q)}(ω)) = ∂R'(ω), so Y − Z_q − S' = ∂R'.
8. (Masses on V.) Let ω be admissible for M_V (tsupport ω ⊆ V, |ω| ≤ 1). Then S'(ω) = S^{(q)}(ω) by (★), and ω is admissible for M; so M_V(S') ≤ M(S^{(q)}). Also M_V(R') ≤ M(R^{(q)}) by monotonicity. Hence M_V(R') + M_V(S') ≤ Σ_i M(R_{q+i}) + Σ_i M(S_{q+i}) = Σ_i (M(R_{q+i}) + M(S_{q+i})) ≤ Σ_i 2^{−(q+i)} = 2·2^{−q}. ∎
proof_key_steps: R^{(q)} := Σ_i R_{q+i} (integer multiplicity, spt ⊆ L) and S^{(q)} := Σ_i S_{q+i} come from the series sibling; their masses sum to at most 2·2^{−q}.
Telescoping: X_{q+N}(ω) → X_q(ω) + ∂R^{(q)}(ω) + S^{(q)}(ω) for every ω.
Hence M(∂R^{(q)}) ≤ 2Λ + M(S^{(q)}) < ∞, and boundary_im makes ∂R^{(q)} integer multiplicity.
On forms supported in V, Y = Z_q + ∂R^{(q)} + S^{(q)}. So S' := Y − Z_q − ∂R^{(q)} is integer multiplicity, Y − Z_q − S' = ∂R^{(q)}, and M_V(R^{(q)}) + M_V(S') ≤ M(R^{(q)}) + M(S^{(q)}) ≤ 2·2^{−q}.

subproblems.title: Locality of approximate tangent spaces, restriction of representations, differences of integer multiplicity currents, orientation bound (reused accepted cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub)
subproblems.statement: (a) Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel sets with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, M has approximate tangent space Q at x (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) if and only if M' does. (b) If U ⊆ ℝ^P is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U (contract structure) and E is Borel, then (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U and it represents some current in 𝒟_n(U). (c) If U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) are integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity), then so is A − B. (d) For every IMRep R in any U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier, |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α (|·| the Euclidean coefficient norm).

Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.im_calculus-a1, status accepted, accepted candidate commit 2af75d6921b01a9c889a45103692ca0af95ea394). It is reused with its identical frozen type; a whitespace-normalised comparison with the declaration in that commit matches, and that commit's only sorry is the frozen root theorem. Role here: It is one of this node's inherited dependencies. Part (c), differences (hence finite integer combinations) of integer multiplicity currents, is used by the node's own assembly (the default decomposition 0, T − T_j) and by the siblings deformation, cauchy_subseq, series and series_limit. Part (b), restriction of a representation to a Borel set, gives the truncations T_j⌞B_{t₀} in localize. Part (a), locality of approximate tangent spaces, is used in series (Simon 3.13). Part (d), the orientation bound, is used in localize. The proof below is the accepted proof of this declaration, copied verbatim.

Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the density argument in the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒” (chapter-03.txt lines 107–160); Ch. 6, Remarks 3.2(1) and 2.9 (chapter-06.txt lines 287–293, 755–768), stated in the book without proof; and Ch. 6, Remark 2.6 for the orientation bound. Hⁿ := μHE[n] throughout. For x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). The statement has four parts: (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces, (b) restriction of a representation to a Borel set, (c) differences of integer multiplicity currents, (d) the orientation bound |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α|; U is open in (a)–(c).

Preliminaries.
(P0) Normalization: SimonGMT's density theorems are stated for simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n, which equals μHE[n] for natural n (SimonGMT Chapter02 simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, with simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure); hence null sets, finiteness and densities transfer verbatim, and Hⁿ is Borel regular (every set has a Borel hull of the same measure).
(P1) Scaling: for every set A, Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(A)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(A) (Mathlib Measure.hausdorffMeasure_smul₀ and invariance of Hausdorff measure under isometries). Hence for Borel A and bounded Borel f, ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} f dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_A f(η_{x,r}(y)) dHⁿ(y).
(P2) Density zero (SimonGMT Chapter01 simon_theorem_3_6, for the Borel regular outer measure Hⁿ, cf. simon_remark_3_7_hausdorff): if D is Borel with Hⁿ(D) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ D, lim_{r↓0} Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ) = 0.
(P3) Cauchy–Binet. For n×P matrices A, B, det(ABᵀ) = Σ_I det(A_I) det(B_I), the sum over increasing I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n) in {1, …, P}, A_I the n×n submatrix of columns I. Proof: the j-th column of ABᵀ is Σ_k B_{jk}A_{·k}, so by multilinearity det(ABᵀ) = Σ_{k_1,…,k_n} B_{1k_1}⋯B_{nk_n} det(A_{·k_1}, …, A_{·k_n}); terms with a repeated index vanish, and grouping the remaining tuples by their underlying increasing tuple I (k = I ∘ σ for a permutation σ) gives Σ_I det(A_I) Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_j B_{j, I_{σ(j)}} = Σ_I det(A_I)det(B_I). (For n > P both sides are 0 — no increasing I, and rank ABᵀ < n.)
(P4) Orientation bound. If τ_1, …, τ_n are orthonormal in ℝ^P and ⟨α, ζ⟩ = ±α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors α, then |⟨α, ζ⟩| ≤ |α| (Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm). Proof: with A_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩, multilinearity and the alternating property give α(τ) = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_I); by Cauchy–Schwarz and (P3), |α(τ)| ≤ |α|(Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2} = |α| det(AAᵀ)^{1/2} = |α|, since AAᵀ = (⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) is the identity. For n = 0, |α(∅)| = |α|.
(P5) Two unit orientations of the same n-dimensional subspace Q differ by a sign: if τ, τ' are orthonormal bases of Q, τ'_i = Σ_j O_{ij}τ_j with O orthogonal, and α(τ') = det(O)α(τ) = ±α(τ) for every alternating α. Hence IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ζ' Q imply ζ' = ζ or ζ' = −ζ, and IsUnitOrientationOf (−ζ) Q holds whenever IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q.
(P6) If R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in an open U, then Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (θ ≥ 1 on M).

(d) Orientation bound. By the orientation field of an IMRep, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier there is Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) Q, i.e. an orthonormal τ with ⟨α, R.orient x⟩ = ±α(τ) for all α; by (P4), |R.orient x α| ≤ |α| for all α. (No openness of U is needed.)

(a) Locality. Let U be open, M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and D := M' ∖ M.
1. For R ∈ ℕ let U_R := {x ∈ U : |x| < R, infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/R} (U_R := {|x| < R} if U = ℝ^P). U_R is open, closure(U_R) is a compact subset of U, and U_R ↑ U. D_R := D ∩ U_R is Borel with Hⁿ(D_R) ≤ Hⁿ(M' ∩ closure(U_R)) < ∞. By (P2) there is an Hⁿ-null set Z_R such that every x ∉ D_R ∪ Z_R satisfies Hⁿ(D_R ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ) as r ↓ 0. Let Z := ⋃_R Z_R, and let Z' ⊇ Z be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0). Let x ∈ M ∖ Z'; choose R with x ∈ U_R and r₀ > 0 with B̄_{r₀}(x) ⊆ U_R. Then x ∉ D_R (as x ∈ M) and D ∩ B̄_r(x) = D_R ∩ B̄_r(x) for r < r₀, so Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ).
2. Fix such x, a subspace Q and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_ρ(0). For r < r₀/ρ the sets η_{x,r}(M), η_{x,r}(M') meet B_ρ(0) in sets of finite Hⁿ-measure, so the integrals below are genuine Bochner integrals. Since η_{x,r} is injective, η_{x,r}(M') is the disjoint union of η_{x,r}(M) and η_{x,r}(D), and by (P1)
 |∫_{η_{x,r}(M')} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ| = |∫_{η_{x,r}(D)} f dHⁿ| ≤ |f|_∞ r^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B_{rρ}(x)) → 0 as r ↓ 0.
Hence for every f the two families of integrals have the same limit as r → 0⁺ or both have none; the condition finrank Q = n is common to both predicates. So HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q for every x ∈ M ∖ Z' and every Q; the exceptional set M ∩ Z' is null for Hⁿ⌞M. ∎

(b) Restriction. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in the open set U and E a Borel set. Define R' with carrier M ∩ E and the same mult θ and orient ξ.
1. Structure fields: M ∩ E is Borel and contained in U; countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono); θ is measurable and θ > 0 on M ∩ E; ∫_{M∩E∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E) ≤ Hⁿ⌞M.
2. Orientation: by (P6) and (a) applied to M ∩ E ⊆ M ⊆ U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ E and all Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ E) x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. With the orientation field of R (Hⁿ-a.e. on M) this gives the orientation field of R'.
3. The current: A(ω) := ∫_{M∩E} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). By (d), |θ⟨ω, ξ⟩| ≤ |ω|_∞ θ 1_{tsupport ω} Hⁿ-a.e. on M, and tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, so the integrand is integrable; A is linear. If ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges: supports in a fixed compact K ⊆ U and uniform convergence of all derivatives, in particular |ω_j|_∞ → 0 since all norms on the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors are equivalent), then |A(ω_j)| ≤ |ω_j|_∞ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ → 0. So A is a GeometricCurrentOn U n and R' represents A (IMRep.Represents, IMRep.action). ∎

(c) Differences. Let A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, be represented by R_A = (M_A, θ_A, ξ_A) and R_B = (M_B, θ_B, ξ_B).
1. (Borel versions and good points.) Choose Borel ξ̃_A, ξ̃_B equal to ξ_A, ξ_B Hⁿ-a.e. on M_A, resp. M_B (a.e. strong measurability; set them 0 off the carriers). By the orientation fields of R_A, R_B, by (P6) and by (a), (M_A ∪ M_B) ∖ G is Hⁿ-null; let N₀ ⊇ (M_A ∪ M_B) ∖ G be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0).
2. (Overlap.) Let x ∈ (M_A ∩ M_B) ∖ N₀. The approximate tangent space of M_A ∩ M_B at x exists and equals Q_A(x) and also Q_B(x) (the equivalences defining G and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces, SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique); so Q_A(x) = Q_B(x) and by (P5) ξ̃_B(x) = ε(x)ξ̃_A(x) with ε(x) ∈ {1, −1}.  M := ((M_A ∖ M_B) ∪ (M_B ∖ M_A) ∪ {x ∈ O : k(x) ≠ 0}) ∖ N₀,
 θ := θ_A on M_A ∖ M_B, θ_B on M_B ∖ M_A, |k| on O, 0 elsewhere (Borel, ℕ-valued),
 ζ := ξ̃_A on M_A ∖ M_B, −ξ̃_B on M_B ∖ M_A, sign(k)ξ̃_A on O, 0 elsewhere (Borel).
For every x ∉ N₀: θ(x)1_M(x)ζ(x) = θ_A(x)1_{M_A}(x)ξ̃_A(x) − θ_B(x)1_{M_B}(x)ξ̃_B(x) (on O with k = 0 both sides vanish; on O with k ≠ 0, θ_Aξ̃_A − θ_Bεξ̃_A = kξ̃_A = |k| sign(k)ξ̃_A; the other cases are immediate).
4. (Representation.) For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), integrating ⟨ω, ·⟩ against both sides of step 3 (N₀ is null; all integrands are integrable by (d), since θ1_M ≤ θ_A1_{M_A} + θ_B1_{M_B}):
 ∫_M θ⟨ω, ζ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_{M_A} θ_A⟨ω, ξ_A⟩ dHⁿ − ∫_{M_B} θ_B⟨ω, ξ_B⟩ dHⁿ = A(ω) − B(ω) = (A − B)(ω).
5. (Structure fields.) M is Borel, M ⊆ M_A ∪ M_B ⊆ U, and M is countably n-rectifiable (countablyRectifiable_iUnion, CountablyRectifiable.mono). θ is Borel and ℕ-valued with θ ≥ 1 on M (|k| ≥ 1 where k ≠ 0), and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M_A∩K} θ_A dHⁿ + ∫_{M_B∩K} θ_B dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U. ζ is Borel, hence a.e. strongly measurable.
6. (Orientation.) For compact K ⊆ U, Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(M_A ∩ K) + Hⁿ(M_B ∩ K) < ∞ by (P6) applied to R_A, R_B. Apply (a) to the pairs (M ∩ M_A ⊆ M_A), (M ∩ M_A ⊆ M), (M ∩ M_B ⊆ M_B), (M ∩ M_B ⊆ M) (all Borel, contained in U, with locally finite Hⁿ-measure): for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ M_A the approximate tangent spaces of M and of M_A at x coincide (both equal that of M ∩ M_A), and similarly for M_B. Let x be such a point, x ∉ N₀. If x ∈ M_A, then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_A(x) and ζ(x) = ±ξ_A(x) (cases M_A ∖ M_B and O, using ξ̃_A(x) = ξ_A(x)), a unit orientation of Q_A(x) by (P5). If x ∈ M_B ∖ M_A, ζ(x) = −ξ_B(x) is a unit orientation of Q_B(x), the approximate tangent space of M at x. Hence the orientation field holds Hⁿ-a.e. on M.
So (M, θ, ζ) is an IMRep in U representing A − B, and A − B is integer multiplicity. ∎

Then for every open W ⊆ U, M_W(T) = μ_R(W), where M_W(T) = T.massOn W is Simon's mass 6.2.5 with the Euclidean coefficient norm (the supremum of T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y) and μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M = R.measure; both sides are taken in [0, ∞].

This child is the comparator-accepted declaration dtc_mass_eq_measure (DAG node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.mass_eq_measure-a1, status accepted, accepted candidate commit bff81d31ecb43002d1bfc77f510d3463c6be155f). It is reused with its identical frozen type; a whitespace-normalised comparison with the declaration in that commit matches, and that commit's only sorry is the frozen root theorem. Role here: It is one of this node's inherited dependencies: fact (MM) of the parent proof, M_V(A) = μ_A(V) for integer multiplicity A and open V. localize uses it for the weights μ_j and the mass of T_j⌞B_{t₀}, deformation for M(P) = Σ|β_F|σⁿ, and series for Simon's identity 3.13 (1). The proof below is the accepted proof of this declaration, copied verbatim.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–766, stated there without proof) together with 2.4–2.8 (lines 222–283); this is the identity "M_W(S) = μ_S(W) for open W" quoted at the start of the parent proof. Notation: for α ∈ Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (Covector), |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(n)})²)^{1/2}, the sum over strictly increasing I : {1,…,n} → {1,…,P}; e^I ∈ Λⁿ is the covector e^I(v₁,…,vₙ) = det(⟨e_{I(a)}, v_b⟩)_{a,b}; μ := μ_R, so μ(B) = ∫_{M∩B} θ dHⁿ for Borel B. By definition M_W(T) = sup{ofReal T(ω) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(y)| ≤ 1 ∀y} ("admissible" forms).
1. Algebraic lemma. Let τ₁,…,τₙ ∈ ℝ^P be orthonormal, σ ∈ {1, −1}, and let ζ ∈ Λₙ (MultiVector) satisfy ζ(α) = σ·α(τ₁,…,τₙ) for all α. For increasing I put d_I := det(⟨e_{I(a)}, τ_b⟩)_{a,b} = e^I(τ₁,…,τₙ). (a) Expanding each τ_b in the standard basis and using multilinearity and the alternating property (terms with a repeated basis vector vanish, the others are grouped by their increasing rearrangement with the sign of the sorting permutation) gives α(τ₁,…,τₙ) = Σ_I α(e_I)·d_I for every α. (b) By the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I d_I² = det(AᵀA), A the P×n matrix with columns τ_b; AᵀA = I_n by orthonormality, so Σ_I d_I² = 1. (c) Hence, by Cauchy–Schwarz, |ζ(α)| = |Σ_I α(e_I)d_I| ≤ |α| for every α. (d) Put α_ζ := Σ_I ζ(e^I)·e^I (a linear function of ζ). Since e^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} for increasing I, J, α_ζ(e_J) = ζ(e^J) = σd_J, hence |α_ζ| = (Σ_J d_J²)^{1/2} = 1 and ζ(α_ζ) = Σ_I ζ(e^I)² = Σ_I d_I² = 1.
2. By the field `orients` of R there is an Hⁿ-null set Z ⊆ M such that for every x ∈ M ∖ Z, ξ(x) satisfies the hypothesis of step 1 (τ an orthonormal basis of the approximate tangent space T_xM). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the function x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable on M (ξ is, ω is continuous, evaluation is continuous bilinear) and bounded by θ(x)·sup|ω|·1_{tsupport ω}(x) off Z; since tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, ∫_{M∩tsupport ω} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (field `locallyIntegrable_mult`). So T(ω) is the integral of an integrable function.
3. Upper bound. Let ω be admissible. For x ∈ M ∖ Z, step 1(c) and tsupport ω ⊆ W give θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) ≤ θ(x)|ω(x)| ≤ θ(x)·1_W(x). Integrating, T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ = μ(W), so ofReal T(ω) ≤ μ(W). Taking the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ(W).
4. Lower bound on a compact set. Let K ⊆ W be compact and 0 < ε < 1. Fix s > 0 with K₁ := {y : dist(y, K) ≤ s} ⊆ W; K₁ is compact, K₁ ⊆ U, so μ(K₁) < ∞.
 (a) The open sets V_m := {dist(·, K) < 1/m} decrease to K and μ(K₁) < ∞, so for some m with 1/m < s the open set V := V_m satisfies K ⊆ V ⊆ K₁ and μ(V ∖ K) < ε.
 (b) Let α(y) := α_{ξ(y)} (step 1(d)); α is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, so there is a Borel map α̃ : ℝ^P → Λⁿ with α̃ = α μ-a.e. Since θ ≥ 1 on M, μ-null subsets of M are Hⁿ-null; let Z' be a Borel Hⁿ-null set containing Z ∪ ({α̃ ≠ α} ∩ M). For y ∈ M ∖ Z' we have |α̃(y)| = 1 and ξ(y)(α̃(y)) = 1. By Lusin's theorem for the finite Borel measure μ⌞K₁ on ℝ^P (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; Λⁿ is identified with ℝ^{C(P,n)} through the coefficients α(e_I)) there is a compact F₀ ⊆ K with μ(K ∖ F₀) < ε/2 and α̃|_{F₀} continuous; by inner regularity there is a compact F ⊆ (F₀ ∩ M) ∖ Z' (a Borel set, M being Borel) with μ(((F₀ ∩ M) ∖ Z') ∖ F) < ε/2. As μ(ℝ^P ∖ M) = 0 and μ(Z') = 0, μ(K ∖ F) < ε; moreover F ⊆ M ∖ Z', α̃|_F is continuous, and |α̃| = 1, ξ(·)(α̃(·)) = 1 on F.
 (c) By the Tietze extension theorem (coefficientwise) α̃|_F extends to a continuous β₀ : ℝ^P → Λⁿ. Let r(v) := v / max(1, |v|), the continuous radial retraction of (Λⁿ, |·|) onto its closed unit ball, and β := r ∘ β₀. Then β is continuous, |β| ≤ 1, and β = α̃ on F (because |α̃| = 1 there).
 (d) Let φ_δ be a standard mollifier (smooth, ≥ 0, ∫φ_δ = 1, support in B_δ(0)) and β_δ := β * φ_δ (coefficientwise convolution). Then β_δ is smooth, |β_δ(y)| ≤ ∫|β(y − z)|φ_δ(z) dz ≤ 1 (convexity of the norm, Minkowski's integral inequality), and β_δ → β uniformly on compact sets as δ ↓ 0 (β is uniformly continuous on compact sets). Fix δ with |β_δ − β| ≤ ε on F.
 (e) Choose χ ∈ C_c^∞(V) with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1 and χ = 1 on K (smooth Urysohn lemma), and set ω := χβ_δ. Then ω is smooth with compact tsupport ⊆ V ⊆ W ⊆ U, so ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and |ω| ≤ 1: ω is admissible.
 (f) Since χ = 1 on F ⊆ K and ω = 0 off V, T(ω) = ∫_{F} θ ξ(β_δ) dHⁿ + ∫_{M∩(V∖F)} θ χ ξ(β_δ) dHⁿ. For y ∈ F (so y ∈ M ∖ Z'): ξ(y)(β_δ(y)) = ξ(y)(α̃(y)) + ξ(y)(β_δ(y) − β(y)) ≥ 1 − |β_δ(y) − β(y)| ≥ 1 − ε by step 1(c) and (b). For y ∈ (M ∩ (V ∖ F)) ∖ Z, |χ(y)ξ(y)(β_δ(y))| ≤ 1. Since μ(V ∖ F) ≤ μ(V ∖ K) + μ(K ∖ F) < 2ε, we get T(ω) ≥ (1 − ε)μ(F) − 2ε ≥ (1 − ε)(μ(K) − ε) − 2ε ≥ μ(K) − ε(μ(K) + 3).
 (g) Hence M_W(T) ≥ ofReal T(ω) ≥ μ(K) − ε(μ(K) + 3); letting ε ↓ 0 gives M_W(T) ≥ μ(K).
5. Exhaustion. W is open, so W = ⋃_m K_m with the increasing compact sets K_m := {y ∈ W : |y| ≤ m, dist(y, ℝ^P ∖ W) ≥ 1/m} (K_m := {|y| ≤ m} if W = ℝ^P). By continuity of μ from below and step 4, μ(W) = sup_m μ(K_m) ≤ M_W(T). Together with step 3, M_W(T) = μ(W) in [0, ∞].
proof_key_steps: A unit simple n-vector ζ satisfies |ζ(α)| ≤ |α|_Euclid (Cauchy–Binet) and has a dual covector α_ζ, linear in ζ, with |α_ζ| = 1 and ζ(α_ζ) = 1.
Upper bound: for every admissible ω, T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ = μ_R(W).
Lower bound on compact K ⊆ W: Lusin, Tietze, radial retraction, mollification and a cutoff give an admissible ω with T(ω) ≥ μ_R(K) − ε(μ_R(K) + 3).
Exhaust the open set W by compact sets to conclude M_W(T) = μ_R(W).

Suppose that for every r ∈ ℕ and every infinite set I ⊆ ℕ there is an infinite set J ⊆ I such that C r j l holds for all j, l ∈ J. Then there is a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ such that C r (φ(r + 1)) (φ(r)) holds for every r ∈ ℕ.

Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration cmc_fc_cs_diagonal_subseq (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.flat_convergence-a1.cauchy_subseq-a1.diagonal_subseq-a1, status accepted, accepted candidate commit b046f226689afca88f2ceb966c9010ac5e581de0). Role here: It is the diagonal argument of step 5 of the parent proof (Simon 7.2, (5)). The sibling cauchy_subseq applies it to the relation 'X_j and X_l are 2^{−r}-close by an integer multiplicity R supported in L'. The proof below is the accepted proof of this declaration, copied verbatim.

Source: steps 4–5 (nested index sets and diagonal choice) of the parent-supplied proof of cmc_fc_cauchy_subseq, i.e. Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2: "apply (1) with ε = 1, 1/2, 1/4 etc. to extract a subsequence {T_{j_r}} … d(T_{j_{r+1}}, T_{j_r}) < 2^{−r}". Here the relation "j and l are 2^{−r}-close" is replaced by an arbitrary relation C r j l.
1. (Choice of refinements.) By the hypothesis and the axiom of choice there is a function F that assigns to each r ∈ ℕ and each infinite I ⊆ ℕ an infinite set F(r, I) ⊆ I such that C r j l for all j, l ∈ F(r, I). Formally, F is a function on the subtype {I : Set ℕ // I.Infinite} with values in the same subtype, obtained by `choose` from the hypothesis.
2. (Nested index sets.) Define I_0 := ℕ (the set univ, which is infinite) and, by recursion on r, I_{r+1} := F(r, I_r). Since F returns infinite sets, every I_r is infinite and the recursion is well defined. By step 1, I_{r+1} ⊆ I_r and C r j l holds for all j, l ∈ I_{r+1}.
3. (Unboundedness.) An infinite set of natural numbers is not bounded above: for every r and every a ∈ ℕ there is b ∈ I_{r+1} with a < b (Set.Infinite.exists_gt). Choose such a b =: g(r, a) for every r and a.
4. (Diagonal choice.) Define φ by recursion: φ(0) := g(0, 0) ∈ I_1 and φ(r + 1) := g(r + 1, φ(r)) ∈ I_{r+2}. Then φ(r) ∈ I_{r+1} for every r, by the choice of g (case r = 0 and case r + 1). Also φ(r) < φ(r + 1) = g(r + 1, φ(r)) for every r. Hence φ is strictly increasing (strictMono_nat_of_lt_succ).
5. (Consecutive terms are related.) Fix r. By step 4, φ(r) ∈ I_{r+1} and φ(r + 1) ∈ I_{r+2}; by step 2, I_{r+2} ⊆ I_{r+1}, so φ(r + 1) ∈ I_{r+1}. Since I_{r+1} = F(r, I_r), step 1 applied to j = φ(r + 1) and l = φ(r) gives C r (φ(r + 1)) (φ(r)). Together with the strict monotonicity of step 4, this proves the claim. ∎

Nested sets: I_0 = ℕ and I_{r+1} = F(r, I_r); all infinite, decreasing, I_{r+1} pairwise C r.
Diagonal choice: φ(r+1) ∈ I_{r+2} with φ(r+1) > φ(r) (Set.Infinite.exists_gt); φ is StrictMono.
φ(r), φ(r+1) ∈ I_{r+1} = F(r, I_r) gives C r (φ(r+1)) (φ(r)).

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 (definition of spt T, chapter-06.txt lines 297–301); the partition-of-unity argument below is the standard reason why the union in 2.11 is itself a set on which the current vanishes. Notation: "S vanishes on W" means S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W.
1. K := tsupport ω is compact and K ⊆ U, because ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is a compactly supported smooth form with tsupport ω ⊆ U. If K = ∅ then ω = 0 and S(ω) = 0 by linearity; assume K ≠ ∅.
2. Since K ⊆ U and K ∩ spt S = ∅, we have K ⊆ U ∖ spt S ⊆ Z_S. By compactness there are finitely many open sets W₁,…,W_m from the family defining Z_S (each with S vanishing on W_i) such that K ⊆ W₁ ∪ … ∪ W_m.
3. Take a smooth partition of unity on ℝ^P subordinate to the open cover {W₁,…,W_m, ℝ^P ∖ K} (e.g. Mathlib's SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate for the closed set K and the cover by W₁,…,W_m): smooth ψ₁,…,ψ_m : ℝ^P → [0,1] with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i for each i and Σ_i ψ_i(y) = 1 for every y ∈ K.
4. For each i, ψ_iω (pointwise product of a smooth function and a smooth n-form) is smooth, and tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ tsupport ψ_i ∩ tsupport ω ⊆ W_i ∩ K; in particular it is compact and contained in U. Thus ψ_iω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ W_i, and S(ψ_iω) = 0 since S vanishes on W_i.
5. ω = Σ_i ψ_iω pointwise: if ω(y) ≠ 0 then y ∈ K and Σ_iψ_i(y) = 1; if ω(y) = 0 both sides vanish. By linearity of S, S(ω) = Σ_i S(ψ_iω) = 0.
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω is a compact subset of the zero region of S, hence covered by finitely many open sets on which S vanishes.
A smooth partition of unity subordinate to this finite cover splits ω into test forms supported in those sets.
Each piece is annihilated by S; linearity gives S(ω) = 0.

Source: parent proof, step 6(f) (“For y ∈ U ∖ K choose s > 0 with B̄_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K … S − T vanishes on all forms supported in B_{s/2}(y), whose closure is compact and contained in U, so y ∉ spt(S − T). Thus spt(S − T) ⊆ K. Being relatively closed in U and contained in the compact K ⊆ U, spt(S − T) is compact”), isolated for an arbitrary current F; the parent applies it to F = S − T.

1. Points of U ∖ K are not in spt F. Let y ∈ U ∖ K. Since U is open and K is closed (compact), U ∖ K is open (IsOpen.sdiff), so there is s > 0 with B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K. Put W := B_{s/2}(y).
 (a) W is open and y ∈ W.
 (b) closure(W) ⊆ B̄_{s/2}(y) ⊆ B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K ⊆ U.
 (c) closure(W) is compact, as a closed subset of the compact closed ball B̄_{s/2}(y) (ℝ^P is proper).
 (d) If ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) and tsupport ω ⊆ W, then tsupport ω ⊆ B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K is disjoint from K, so F(ω) = 0.
 By (a)-(d), W is one of the sets whose union is Z(F), so y ∈ Z(F) and y ∉ spt F.

2. spt F ⊆ K. By definition spt F ⊆ U, and by step 1 no point of U ∖ K lies in spt F.

3. Compactness. From spt F = U ∖ Z(F), spt F ⊆ K and K ⊆ U, we get spt F = K ∖ Z(F). Z(F) is open, as a union of open sets (isOpen_zeroRegion). So K ∖ Z(F) is a closed subset of the compact set K, hence compact (IsCompact.diff). ∎

Hence spt F ⊆ K, and spt F = K ∖ Z(F) is compact because Z(F) is open.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 4.10 and the remark preceding it (chapter-06.txt lines 1367–1376: M_W(T⌞{f<t}) is increasing in t, hence differentiable for L¹-a.e. t, ∫_a^b (d/dt)M_W(T⌞{f<t}) dt ≤ M_W(T⌞{a<f<b}), and 4.9 gives 4.10), and step 4 of the parent proof; μ(W ∩ {a < f < s}) plays the role of M_W(T⌞{a<f<s}) and m(t) that of M_W(⟨T, f, t₋⟩). Write S_h(t) := {x : t − h < f(x) < t} and N := μ(W ∩ {a < f < b}).
1. (Trivial cases.) If b ≤ a then Ioo a b = ∅ and the left side is 0. If L = 0, the hypothesis gives m(t) ≤ 0·(…) = 0 for every t ∈ (a, b) (in [0, ∞], 0·∞ = 0), so m = 0 a.e. for volume restricted to Ioo a b (ae_restrict_iff' with measurableSet_Ioo) and the left side is 0 (lintegral_mono_ae). If L > 0 and N = ∞, the right side is ∞. Assume from now on a < b and N < ∞.
2. (Distribution function.) For s ∈ ℝ let E_s := W ∩ {a < f < min(s, b)} and F(s) := (μ(E_s)).toReal. If s ≤ s' then E_s ⊆ E_{s'}, and μ(E_s) ≤ μ(E_b) = N < ∞; hence F is real valued and monotone on ℝ, ofReal(F(s)) = μ(E_s), F(s) = 0 for s ≤ a (then E_s = ∅) and F(b) = N.toReal.
3. (Strip estimate.) Let t ∈ (a, b) and 0 < h < t − a. E_t = W ∩ {a < f < t} is the disjoint union of W ∩ {a < f ≤ t − h} and W ∩ S_h(t), and W ∩ S_h(t) is measurable (W and f are measurable). By additivity (measure_union), μ(E_t) = μ(W ∩ {a < f ≤ t − h}) + μ(W ∩ S_h(t)) ≥ μ(E_{t−h}) + μ(W ∩ S_h(t)), because E_{t−h} = W ∩ {a < f < t − h} ⊆ W ∩ {a < f ≤ t − h} (note t − h < b). All terms are finite, so μ(W ∩ S_h(t)) ≤ ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)) and ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ(W ∩ S_h(t)) ≤ ofReal((F(t) − F(t − h))/h).
4. (Differentiation.) F is monotone, so by Lebesgue's theorem (Monotone.ae_differentiableAt) it is differentiable at a.e. t ∈ ℝ. Let t ∈ (a, b) be such a point. By hasDerivAt_iff_tendsto_slope, (F(s) − F(t))/(s − t) → deriv F t as s → t, s ≠ t; with s = t − h and h → 0+ this says (F(t) − F(t − h))/h → deriv F t, hence ofReal((F(t) − F(t − h))/h) → ofReal(deriv F t). By step 3 (valid for all h ∈ (0, t − a), i.e. eventually in 𝓝[>]0), liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ(W ∩ S_h(t)) ≤ ofReal(deriv F t), and by hypothesis m(t) ≤ L·ofReal(deriv F t). Thus m(t) ≤ L·ofReal(deriv F t) for a.e. t ∈ (a, b).
5. (Integration.) By lintegral_mono_ae (valid for arbitrary, not necessarily measurable, functions) for volume restricted to Ioo a b, and lintegral_const_mul' (L ≠ ∞), ∫⁻_{(a,b)} m ≤ ∫⁻_{(a,b)} L·ofReal(deriv F t) dt = L·∫⁻_{(a,b)} ofReal(deriv F t) dt. deriv F ≥ 0 everywhere (Monotone.deriv_nonneg) and deriv F is integrable on [a, b] (MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv), so ∫⁻_{(a,b)} ofReal(deriv F) = ofReal(∫_{(a,b)} deriv F) (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal), and ∫_{(a,b)} deriv F = ∫_{(a,b]} deriv F = ∫_a^b deriv F (integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo, intervalIntegral.integral_of_le) ≤ F(b) − F(a) = N.toReal (MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc, uIcc a b = [a, b], F(a) = 0). Hence ∫⁻_{(a,b)} m ≤ L·ofReal(N.toReal) = L·N, since N < ∞. ∎

F(s) := μ(W ∩ {a < f < min(s, b)}).toReal is monotone and μ(W ∩ {t−h<f<t}) ≤ F(t) − F(t−h) for t ∈ (a, b), 0 < h < t − a.
At a.e. t (Lebesgue: monotone F is differentiable a.e.) the liminf is ≤ F'(t), so m(t) ≤ L·F'(t) a.e. on (a, b).
